title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 24
statement: Let \(ABCDEF\) be a regular hexagon with side length \(1.\) Denote by \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) the midpoints of sides \(AB,\) \(CD,\) and \(EF,\) respectively. What is the area of the convex hexagon whose interior is the intersection of the interiors of \(\triangle ACE\) and \(\triangle XYZ?\)

solutions.text:
The triangle \(XYZ\) is equilateral with side \(\frac{3}{2},\) so its area is \[\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\left(\dfrac32\right)^2=\dfrac{9\sqrt3}{16}.\]

The triangles \(ACE\) and \(XYZ\) are concentric and rotated \(30^\circ\) from each other. At each vertex of \(XYZ,\) the sides of \(ACE\) cut off a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90\) triangle whose hypotenuse is the half-side segment \(AX=\frac{1}{2}.\) Its legs are \(\frac{1}{4}\) and \(\frac{\sqrt3}{4},\) so each corner has area \(\frac{\sqrt3}{32}.\)

Removing the three corners gives \[\dfrac{9\sqrt3}{16}-3\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{32}=\dfrac{15\sqrt3}{32}.\] Therefore, the answer is C.
hints: \(\triangle ACE\) is equilateral with side \(\sqrt{3};\) \(\triangle XYZ\) is equilateral with side \(\tfrac{3}{2}\)
Centered at the hexagon’s center the two triangles are concentric and rotated \(30^\circ;\) the overlap is \(\triangle XYZ\) minus its three protruding corner triangles
